name: FRED (Framework for Reconstructing Epidemic Dynamics)
description: Open-source agent-based epidemic simulation framework developed at the University of Pittsburgh Public Health Dynamics Laboratory. Uses census-based synthetic populations to model disease spread through realistic household, school, workplace, and community contact networks. Each agent follows individual disease progression and behavioral rules, producing emergent population-level epidemic curves. Validated against real outbreak data for influenza, COVID-19, and other infectious diseases.
general_score_metric: scenario-specific epidemiological metrics (e.g., RMSE of incidence time series, attack-rate error, peak-timing error)
reputation: Respected open-source epidemiological ABM; used by CDC and NIH-funded research groups
notes: Open source; available on GitHub. Uses RTI International synthetic population data. Supports customizable disease models and intervention policies. Primary use case is U.S. county-level epidemic simulation.

institutions: University of Pittsburgh Public Health Dynamics Laboratory
